blocks.0: CHANGE OF NAME – EVENVIK TO GULEN
blocks.1: “Evenvik parish, sub-parish and municipality shall be called Gulen parish, sub-parish and municipality.”
blocks.2: So says the royal decree of 17 May 1890. This decision came after extensive discussions and consultations in connection with a reorganisation of the bailiwicks of Sogn, Sunnfjord and Nordfjord in the second half of the nineteenth century.
blocks.3: In connection with a letter from the “Ministry of Finance and Customs” to the county governor of Nordre Bergenhus county dated 10 May 1878, the head of the ministry held that “it must be considered expedient that, at the same time as the negotiations on the above-mentioned reorganisation, it be considered whether the name of the court district concerned, when it differed from that of the parish or sub-parishes of which the court district consisted, ought to be changed so as to agree with it”.
blocks.4: This was the start, on the authorities' side, of the process of changing the name as far as our municipality was concerned.
blocks.5: In a “submission” from the county governor to the ministry “of 6 March 1879 concerning the change of the names of a number of parishes, sub-parishes, municipalities and court districts within the county, regarding which there is disagreement between the ecclesiastical and the secular division”, 11 districts in our county are mentioned, and Gulen is among them.
blocks.6: The county governor obtained “the statements of the municipal councils concerned as to whether they have any objection to the court districts being given the same names as the parishes”. There were no great objections around the county, “whereas Evenvik municipal council has spoken against changing the name of either the court district or the parish.” In other words, the municipal council here did not want anything changed.
blocks.7: The people of Solund, who at that time, as the last of the annexes, were about to be separated from Eivindvik parish, wished their name to be “Solundøerne” (the Solund islands) for both the court district and the parish, “should such a parish be established there”. In his statement the district judge of Ytre Sogn recommended that Gulen as the name of the court district “be retained instead of Evindvik” and that “Utvær court district be called the Solund Islands court district”. The bailiff had no comment on the question of the name here.
blocks.8: The usual practice around the country was for the names of court districts to be changed to match the name of the parish or main sub-parish. The county governor's proposal to the ministry contained changes that went against this. Thus, among other things, “Klævold municipality and court district” was proposed changed to “Kirkebø municipality and court district”, and “Evindvik sub-parish, parish and municipality to be called Gulen sub-parish, parish and municipality”.
blocks.9: The ministry sent the county governor's proposal for assessment to a “Commission for the Revision of the Spelling of Place Names”, appointed by royal decree of 11 April 1878, which in a letter of 1 July 1880 made 5 comments. Comments no. 1 and 2 concern our case and read as follows:
blocks.10: The commission is inclined to prefer the names Kirkebø municipality and court district to Klævold municipality and court district, because sub-parish names as well as parish names must generally be assumed to be far better known than the names of court districts, which are seldom used in daily life. For this reason too, as far as the commission is aware, in the many similar changes of name made in various parts of the country in recent times, the names of court districts have everywhere regularly had to give way to the names of parishes, or in some cases sub-parishes.
blocks.11: For the same reason the commission also believes it ought to recommend changing the name Gulen court district to Evindvik court district, instead of, as proposed by the county governor, changing Evindvik parish and municipality to Gulen parish and municipality. The commission admits, moreover, that the name Gulen, through the historical memories attached to the place as the old site of the Gulating, has become better known than similar names in general, and that there could thus be more to be said here for preferring the name of the court district than in the previous case.”
blocks.12: Comment no. 3 concerns Solund, where the commission concluded by proposing “the names Sulen sub-parish, municipality and court district”. Comment no. 4 concerned Indre and Ytre Holmedal, and comment no. 5 concerned Selje. Apart from these comments, the commission found “that it could support the county governor's proposal”.
blocks.13: The “Ministry of Justice” made no comment concerning Gulen. The statement from the “Ministry of the Interior” says concerning Gulen: “that the name Gulen parish, municipality and court district is, in the ministry's opinion, to be preferred to Evindvik parish etc., both because of the historical memories attached to that name and because of its form.”
blocks.14: Before giving its “opinion”, the “Ministry of Church Affairs” had obtained statements from the priests in “Ladvik, Evindvik and Sælø, the deans of the Ytre Sogn and Nordfjord deaneries and the Bergen diocesan board”.
blocks.15: The parish priest here at that time was Jakob Andreas Wille Sandberg (he came here in 1879 and left in 1893). He “remarks in his statement of 16 October 1884 that he has nothing essential to say against Evindvik sub-parish, parish and municipality being called Gulen sub-parish, parish and municipality.” It has not been possible to obtain a copy of this letter from Sandberg, but the ministry's account shows that even though people did say “Evindvik sub-parish” and “will probably go on saying it, even if the name is officially changed”, the parish priest believed that the name Gulen was “more common among the common people than Evindvik as the name of the district corresponding to the main sub-parish.”
blocks.16: The account goes on: “Perhaps the intended change of name could take effect from the time when the parish will include no more than Gulen proper, or in other words from the time when the annexes are separated and become a parish of their own.”
blocks.17: As for Utvær, which still came under Eivindvik parish, it appears that the parish priest supports the name “Sulen” rather than “Solundøerne”. He believes that “Solundøerne” is cumbersome and will, if adopted, “be used only on paper”. The parish priest believes that old place names no longer “used in the mouths of the people” should not be revived for official use, and that in any case the names that are revived should not differ so much from “the forms current in the spoken language that they seem unnatural.”
blocks.18: The dean of Ytre Sogn gave as his opinion that Eivindvik parish should be changed to Gulen parish from the time “Sulen parish is established, ‘Sulen’ is kept and Utvær municipality is changed to Sulen municipality.”
blocks.19: The “Bergen diocesan board” also recommended that our parish change its name to Gulen parish.
blocks.20: After all these statements the “Ministry of Church Affairs” then declared, among other things, “that Gulen parish, municipality and court district, for the reasons emphasised by the said ministry, ought to be preferred to Evindvik parish, municipality and court district.” “The said ministry” was in this case the “Ministry of the Interior”.
blocks.21: The documents in the case were later put before “the chairman of the Names Commission, Professor Rygh”, who, together with one of his colleagues on the commission, Professor Sophus Bugge, gave the following opinion on the question of Gulen – Eivindvik:
blocks.22: “As regards the question of Evindvik or Gulen, the professor still holds to the opinion expressed by the Names Commission in its statement of 1 July 1880, that the name Evindvik (or, as it will be written in the new land register in closer agreement with the present pronunciation, Evenvik) should be preferred for practical reasons. In the professor's view the name Evenvik is at present so much better known than Gulen that less inconvenience will follow from changing the name of the court district and sheriff's district to Evenvik than, conversely, from changing the name of the parish to Gulen. The professor also draws attention to the fact that the name Gulen no doubt originally belongs to the fjord of that name that cuts into the mainland part of the parish, and that there is another, if perhaps somewhat less known, fjord called Gulen in the diocese of Bergen – in Bremanger parish.”
blocks.23: As can be seen, many points were raised both for and against a change of name. After an overall assessment the “Ministry of Finance and Customs” finally made its recommendation on 29 April 1890. It says:
blocks.24: “Evenvik parish, sub-parish and municipality are to be called Gulen, like the sheriff's district and the court district. In this regard it should be noted that the ministry has been in doubt as to whether the said change should take place, or whether conversely the name Gulen should be replaced by Evenvik. All the authorities have, as stated above, spoken in favour of the first-mentioned change, with the exception of the municipal council, which is against any change, and the Names Commission, which holds that Evenvik should be preferred. In these circumstances, and since the parish priest concerned has stated that the name Gulen is more common among the common people than Evenvik as the name of the district corresponding to the main sub-parish, the ministry has thought it right to follow the opinion of the majority.”
blocks.25: The draft resolution says: “On the basis of the foregoing, with which the other members of the Council of State essentially agree, it is most humbly recommended:
blocks.26: That the following changes with regard to the names of a number of court districts and sheriff's districts etc. in Nordre Bergenhus county be most graciously decided to take effect from 1 July 1890:
blocks.28: Evenvik parish, sub-parish and municipality shall be called Gulen parish, sub-parish and municipality.”
blocks.29: The proposal was confirmed as a royal decree by King Oscar II on 17 May 1890, and the old and once so far-reaching parish had a new name – GULEN!
